summary: Every measured limb of the acceptance criterion passes, and I re-measured all of it myself rather than trusting the coordinator table: 49/49 baseline source pins match live bytes, 41/41 status-evidence pins match, all 13 required selectors resolve with exactly the stated values, and all six pinned executions reproduce including both EP13 stdout digests and the SELFTEST-PASS banner. No stop-class name/digest conflict exists anywhere, which I established over all 15 claim bindings rather than the 9 the draft names. DR-204 is ACCEPTED, so the D-001 gate is open, and the EVIDENCE v10-versus-v15 question is a recorded two-level structure the freeze, register and matrix all agree on, not a conflict. I nonetheless return NOT-SATISFIED-GRADE on one blocker, and it is not about the measurements. The proposed file-08 lead installs `SATISFIED 2026-08-14` into a cell whose retained text states, twice, that readiness condition 1 nets to zero SATISFIED rows until this very re-record lands, and one of those sentences also asserts the row's LIVE standing is OPEN. The draft does not dispose of either. That is the mirror image of the exact defect this cell was corrected for on 2026-08-13, with the correction note still sitting in it.

blockersList.location: Proposed file-08 live lead, against the retained text of file 08's DR-001 cell (line 34)
blockersList.claim: The proposed lead would install a SATISFIED lead over retained text that asserts the row's live standing is OPEN and that condition 1 nets to zero SATISFIED rows until this re-record lands. The draft disposes of neither sentence, so the cell would contradict itself on live standing.
evidence: File 08's DR-001 cell is a single 5928-character row at line 34. It contains 'nets to zero SATISFIED rows' twice.
Occurrence 1, bolded: '**readiness condition 1 nets to zero `SATISFIED` rows until that re-record lands.**'

Occurrence 2, and the more serious one because it states live standing in the present tense: 'the row's LIVE standing is **OPEN** pending regeneration plus independent review under the D-001 two-stage rule, sequenced before C-final. Readiness condition 1 therefore nets to zero `SATISFIED` rows until that re-record lands.'

The proposed lead reads '**SATISFIED 2026-08-14.**' and its carry-list disposes of R1-R3, R4(a)-(d) and R5. It says nothing about either 'nets to zero' sentence or about the 'LIVE standing is OPEN' clause.

The same cell already carries the record of this defect being corrected once: '*(Lead corrected 2026-08-13: this cell previously led with `SATISFIED 2026-08-12` while its own tail recorded the re-open — condition 1 is evaluated over row status, so the lead must read the live standing. The dispositions below stand as history, unedited and superseded rather than rewritten.)*'
blockersList.whyThisIsABlockerAndNotAnAdvisory: The dispatch asks me to grade whether the criterion is met 'such that a file-08-only SATISFIED re-record would be lawful'. The lawfulness of the recording is inside the question, not adjacent to it. As drafted, the recording produces a cell that says SATISFIED in its lead and 'the row's LIVE standing is OPEN' in its body — and the register's own correction note states the governing rule that makes this fatal: condition 1 is evaluated over row status, so the lead must read the live standing. A reader reconciling the two would have to infer that 'that re-record' names the act in the lead and that the sentence is therefore spent. The 2026-08-13 correction exists precisely because that inference must not be required.
blockersList.iConsideredTheCounterArgument: The phrase 'until that re-record lands' is a temporal qualifier that arguably retires itself once the re-record lands, which would make both sentences self-limiting rather than false. I do not think that saves it. The second occurrence is not qualified in the same way — 'the row's LIVE standing is **OPEN**' is a present-tense assertion of standing with no temporal escape, and it would sit under a SATISFIED lead. And a self-limiting sentence still reads as live text in a live cell; D-044 faced the identical situation with 'A baseline refresh re-opens it' and did not rely on self-limitation, it named the sentences and retired them.
blockersList.remedy: Extend the proposed lead in D-044 clause 2's established form: name both occurrences of 'readiness condition 1 nets to zero `SATISFIED` rows until that re-record lands' and the 'the row's LIVE standing is **OPEN**' clause, state that they cease to be live standing and remain history, and state the new condition-1 accounting — DR-001 becomes the first SATISFIED row of the eleven, and condition 1 still does not discharge. Note that both occurrences must be retired, not one: this is the same two-occurrence trap I recorded as NOTE-C2-D044-01 against D-044's scope-clause rewrite.
blockersList.whatWouldClearIt: A corrected draft carrying that disposition would, on the measurements I made, grade SATISFIED-GRADE. Nothing I measured about the criterion itself fails.

advisoriesList.observation: The row lists nine binding artifacts as checked. The claim register carries fifteen. The nine are exactly the nine that carry a `bindingArtifactSha256`; the other six -- C-1, TM, RESOLVED-INPUTS, DELIVERY, FACT-IDENTITY, FACT-PLANE -- have a bindingArtifact path and no pinned digest, so no name/digest pair exists to conflict.
advisoriesList.whyItIsNotABlocker: The selection is principled rather than a coverage gap, which I established by testing all fifteen myself before concluding. The stop-class test can only fire where a digest exists, and it fires nowhere.
advisoriesList.whyItIsWorthRecording: As written a reader takes the nine as the population of binding artifacts. It is the population of digest-pinned ones. For a SATISFIED-grade row the denominator matters: stating 'nine of fifteen bindings carry a pinned digest; those nine match; the remaining six are name-only and cannot conflict' would make the sweep's completeness checkable instead of inferable.

verdictNote: NOT-SATISFIED-GRADE, on one blocker, and I want the shape of this on the record because it is not a measurement failure. Every limb of the acceptance criterion passes and I re-derived all of it myself: 49/49, 41/41, 13/13, 6/6 executions with both EP13 stdout digests reproducing, no stop-class conflict across all fifteen claim bindings, DR-204 open as the gate, and the EVIDENCE v10 binding correct under the authorityRule's own instruction not to select a newer-looking file. If the criterion were the whole question I would return SATISFIED-GRADE. The dispatch asks something more: whether a file-08-only SATISFIED re-record would be LAWFUL. The proposed lead would write SATISFIED into a cell that still says, in the present tense, that the row's live standing is OPEN and that condition 1 nets to zero SATISFIED rows until this re-record lands, and it disposes of neither sentence. That cell was corrected on 2026-08-13 for the mirror image of this defect, and the correction note explaining why is still inside it. One clause in D-044's retirement form clears it, and both occurrences must be named rather than one.
